title: Recipes and a Team Capstone —

header.html: Fix the nine most common mistakes with the exact commands (wrong branch, pushed too early, messy history, lost commit, wrong message, big file, detached HEAD, bad merge, diverged pull); run a full team workflow with a shared remote, feature branches, a conflict, no-ff and squash merges, a release tag and a hotfix; check a team repository against a final checklist
Git 2.50.1: every command was run in the lab

toc.title: The team simulation: who does what
The final checklist for a team repository

html:
1Recipes for common mistakes

Everybody makes these mistakes, and every one of them has a short fix. The commands come from modules 3 to 7. The question to ask first is always the same: has the commit left my computer? Before a push you may rewrite. After a push, undo with a new commit.

Mistake Fix Watch out
Committed on the wrong branch git switch -c feature/cart, then git branch -f main origin/main Before you push; the commit moves to the new branch
Pushed too early git revert HEAD, then git push Adds an undo commit; no force push needed
Messy history git rebase -i HEAD~3, mark the later commits fixup, then git commit --amend for the message Only for commits nobody else has
Lost a commit git reflog, then git reset --hard HEAD@{1} The reflog lives in your clone only
Wrong commit message git commit --amend -m "Add login form" Only before the push
Big file committed git rm --cached big.bin, add it to .gitignore, then git commit --amend After a push see module 15: rotate or rewrite
Detached HEAD git switch -c rescue Do it before you switch away
Merge went wrong In conflict: git merge --abort. Merged, not pushed: git reset --hard ORIG_HEAD ORIG_HEAD is where HEAD was before the merge
Pull diverged git pull --rebase for a straight line, or git pull --no-rebase for a merge commit A plain git pull stops and asks you to choose
Tip

. Use git revert for anything already pushed to a shared branch, and keep reset for commits that only you have. A revert adds history; a reset removes it for you and breaks the clones of everyone else.

Tip

. Run git reflog before you panic. It lists where HEAD has been, so a commit lost by a reset is usually one command away.

2The team simulation: who does what

The capstone demonstration plays a whole team in one temporary folder. Nothing is shared except a local bare repository, which stands in for the repository on GitHub.

Who Role
origin The bare repository that everybody pushes to and pulls from
Ada The maintainer: merges the finished branches and tags the releases
Bob Works on prices; meets a conflict and resolves it on his own branch
Cy Works on search; later fixes a typo from the release tag

Each person starts with a clone and works on a feature branch: feature/cart, feature/prices and feature/search. Ada and Bob both changed the price line of shop.txt, so the second merge is bound to conflict.

The first block shows Ada merging the cart with --no-ff, which keeps a merge commit as the visible record of the pull request. Then Bob brings origin/main into his own branch. Your hashes will differ.

git switch main                                          # Ada
git pull
git merge --no-ff -m "Merge cart" origin/feature/cart
git push
git fetch                                                # Bob, on feature/prices
git merge origin/main
# Bob edits shop.txt: keeps price=12, removes the marker lines
git add shop.txt
git commit -m "Resolve price conflict"
git push

Auto-merging shop.txt
CONFLICT (content): Merge conflict in shop.txt
Automatic merge failed; fix conflicts and then commit the result.

The conflict output belongs to Bob's merge. Bob resolves it on his own branch, so the maintainer's main never sees a broken state.

Tip

. Resolve a conflict on your own branch: merge the target branch into it, fix the file, then let the maintainer merge a clean branch. Nobody else is blocked while you work.

3Merge, squash, release and hotfix

Ada now merges Bob's branch with --no-ff and the search branch with --squash. A squash merge turns the two search commits into one new commit with a single parent. The original commits stay on the feature branch but not on main. Then Ada tags the release.

git switch main
git pull
git merge --no-ff -m "Merge prices" origin/feature/prices
git merge --squash origin/feature/search
git commit -m "Add search"
git tag -a v1.0 -m "Release 1.0"
git push origin main v1.0

A bug appears in the release. Cy starts the hotfix from the tag, not from main, because main may hold work that is not released yet. Ada merges the fix and tags it.

git fetch --tags                                          # Cy
git switch -c hotfix/typo v1.0
git commit -am "Fix cart typo"                            # after fixing the typo
git push -u origin hotfix/typo
git fetch                                                 # Ada
git switch main
git merge --no-ff -m "Merge hotfix" origin/hotfix/typo
git tag -a v1.0.1 -m "Hotfix 1.0.1"
git push origin main v1.0.1
git log --first-parent --oneline
git tag -l

eb58d87 Merge hotfix
7eac700 Add search
c732586 Merge prices
0f21a8f Merge cart
306b842 Add shop file
v1.0
v1.0.1

The lab asserts the shape of this history. The first-parent line of main has five commits, one per unit of work. Three of them are merges, and Bob's conflict resolution makes four merge commits in all. The squash commit has one parent.

Both tags are annotated, v1.0 is an ancestor of v1.0.1, and the three clones end on the same commit as origin.

Tip

. Branch a hotfix from the release tag, not from main. The fix then contains exactly what you shipped, plus one change.

4The final checklist for a team repository

  • Start clean. Pull before you start and branch from an up-to-date main.
  • One change, one branch. Give it a short, descriptive name.
  • Commit well. Small commits with a message that says why (module 12).
  • Use a pull request. Push the branch, open a pull request and link the issue.
  • Wait for green and for a review. Checks and approvals come before the merge (modules 9 and 11).
  • Fix conflicts on your branch. Never settle them with a force push.
  • Leave shared history alone. Rewrite only commits nobody has, and use --force-with-lease, never plain --force.
  • Choose the merge method on purpose. Merge commit, squash or rebase, as the team agreed.
  • Tag releases, hotfix from tags. Annotated tags such as v1.0 mark what shipped.
  • Keep it safe. No secrets in commits, a protected main, and signed commits if the team asks (module 15).

5Practice Q&A

5.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1A wrong commit is already on the shared main that teammates have pulled. What is the safest way to undo it?

  • ARun git reset --hard HEAD~1, then force push
  • BRun git revert HEAD, then push normally
  • CRun git commit --amend, then force push
  • DDelete the remote main and push it again
Show the answer

Answer: B. A revert adds a new commit and rewrites nothing, so the clones of your teammates stay valid.

S2A pull ends with "Need to specify how to reconcile divergent branches". What does this output tell you?

  • AThe remote branch was deleted and must be created again
  • BYour clone has no upstream branch configured for this branch
  • CThe pull was blocked because the working tree is not clean
  • DBoth sides have new commits, so you must choose rebase or merge
Show the answer

Answer: D. The branches diverged, so choose git pull --rebase or git pull --no-rebase.

S3You ran git reset --hard HEAD~1 and a day of work disappeared. Nothing was pushed. What brings it back?

  • Agit reflog, then git reset --hard HEAD@{1}
  • Bgit revert HEAD, because the reset was a commit
  • Cgit fetch, because the remote still has it
  • Dgit stash pop, because reset saves a stash
Show the answer

Answer: A. The reflog still lists the lost commit, and resetting to its entry restores it.

S4You made two commits on main by mistake and have not pushed. What moves them to a new branch and cleans main?

  • Agit branch -d main, then git switch -c feature/cart
  • Bgit revert HEAD~2..HEAD, then git push origin main
  • Cgit switch -c feature/cart, then git branch -f main origin/main
  • Dgit stash, then git switch -c feature/cart and git stash pop
Show the answer

Answer: C. The new branch keeps the commits, and moving main back to origin/main removes them from it.

S5Cy's branch has two commits, and Ada squash merges it into main. What does main show afterwards?

  • ABoth commits, plus a merge commit with two parents
  • BBoth commits in a straight line, with no merge commit at all
  • COne new commit with one parent, and no trace of the two
  • DOne new commit with two parents, one for each source commit
Show the answer

Answer: C. A squash merge creates a single new commit, and the original commits stay on the feature branch only.

S6v1.0 shipped last week and main holds newer unreleased work. A bug needs a quick fix for production. Where should the hotfix branch start?

  • AFrom the newest commit on main, which has the latest code
  • BFrom the first commit of the repository, to keep it small
  • CFrom the feature branch with the most recent commits
  • DFrom the v1.0 tag, which is exactly what shipped
Show the answer

Answer: D. A hotfix from the release tag contains only the shipped code plus the one fix.

5.2 Recall questions

R1Which command undoes a pushed commit without rewriting history?

Show the answer

git revert.

R2Which command lists where HEAD has been, to find a lost commit?

Show the answer

git reflog.

R3What does git merge --abort do?

Show the answer

It stops a conflicted merge and restores the branch to the state before it.

R4Which merge option forces a merge commit even when a fast-forward is possible?

Show the answer

--no-ff.

R5How do you create an annotated tag for a release?

Show the answer

git tag -a v1.0 -m "Release 1.0".

R6Which push option is safer than --force?

Show the answer

--force-with-lease.

6Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
First question has the commit left my computer? Not pushed: rewrite. Pushed: revert
Wrong branch git switch -c feature/cart, then git branch -f main origin/main
Lost or wrong git reflog and git reset --hard HEAD@{1}; git commit --amend; git switch -c rescue for a detached HEAD
Merge trouble git merge --abort in conflict; git reset --hard ORIG_HEAD after an unpushed merge
Diverged pull git pull --rebase for a line, git pull --no-rebase for a merge commit
Merge styles --no-ff keeps a merge commit; --squash makes one single-parent commit
Release and hotfix git tag -a v1.0; hotfix branch from the tag; tag the fix v1.0.1
Team habits feature branches, pull requests, green checks, no shared rewrites, no secrets
